title: A dark playable browser fable made on a $20 Claude subscription (Three.js / R3F)(sound on)
author: Acrobatic_Mush
selftext:
Play in the browser: https://ragnaroklamb.itch.io/lamb or https://ragnarok-lamb.vercel.app/lamb

I’m a software engineer, not a traditional game dev. I’m building Ragnarok Lamb, a dark fable browser boss rush where a black lamb walks a forest road, fights flying monkeys, and enters five boss dimensions that each warp a fundamental law of physics.

The lore, art direction, weapon choices, combat tactics, and physics are 100% mine. I wanted to turn my lore into a game quickly, at the absolute minimum cost possible and without it looking like total shit. 

Here is a breakdown of how I am building:

1. The 3D Toolchain

Procedural Meshes: Started fully procedural from 2D concept sheets. Good baseline, but lacked punch for hero models.

img2threejs: Changed the Bosses completely.

Tripo3D: Sucks at anything that doesn't resemble a standard humanoid and my hero is a quad.

Hyper3D: Significantly better geometry and topology, though it lacks native animation pipelines.

Mixamo: Great for fast humanoid rigs, but useless for custom winged creatures without workarounds.

No Blender: I wanted it fast with minimal dependencies instead of sinking weeks into manual DCC workflows or paying extra for AI skills. Though might use it if I add another dimension or refactor current.

2. Multi-Agent Development Pipeline

I structured the build like an engineering team on a standard $20 sub:

Lead Architect: Opus 5.5 drives the sim, scene graphs,VFX and complex physics loops.

The Workhorses: Grok, Gemini, and Codex (Luna) handle high-iteration boilerplate, quick scripts, shader variations, and refactoring or when I do multiple visual passes to decide on a look.

The Reviewer: Opus 5.5 again, auditing performance and reviewing other agent's work. The lamb went from 142 draw calls to 1 by replacing the procedural model with a single baked sculpt mesh, and each flying monkey from 247 meshes to 44 draws by merging.

3. Audio & Voices

Free credited asset packs for sound effects and music.

Flying monkey chatters and taunts generated via Gemini TTS. Created a small app for that.

It took multiple iterations to get the flowers to look like flowers & not fried egg. Still working on VFX effects whenever I get time.

Happy to answer questions about the setup or the agent workflows and which AI does what better!

Please share your feedback in comments.
